content.text:
I found two claims the record doesn't support; everything else checks out.

1. **Contributing factor 1** says every flag evaluation was on within the onset minute. The 09:07 log line (G971b) shows 72 off and 128 on. Evaluations were only all on from 09:08 (Gce95).
2. **Causal chain step 3** says `render_spend_summary` sends any request with the monthly summary selected to the failing function. It leaves out a condition: the code at the running revision (S1) checks `use_typical_spend` first. Only requests without the typical-spend rollout reach the monthly function, which Code-Fix also says in F1.

Neither went_wrong item is something that field excludes. The rollback was blocked by the platform answering 503, not refused by Argus, and the missed page is a finding of its own. I left out the "had it been otherwise" what-ifs and the action items, since those aren't judged.

flags.quote: Within the onset minute every evaluation was on, and no gradual ramp was seen.
flags.why: In the onset minute 09:07, 72 evaluations were off and 128 on; all evaluations were on only from 09:08.

flags.quote: render_spend_summary sends any request with the monthly summary selected to that function
flags.why: At the running revision, render_spend_summary sends a request to the monthly function only when use_monthly_summary is true and use_typical_spend is false; typical spend takes precedence.

supported.quote: Revision 383534e removed the guard in average_spend_per_item_this_month that handled a shopper with no purchases this month. It also changed the function to decide 'this month' from each purchase's recorded_at.

The function now divides the month's total by the number of purchases recorded this month with nothing to handle an empty month, so it raises ZeroDivisionError for any shopper with no purchase recorded this month.

A software update took out the protection for shoppers who had bought nothing so far this month, so when a new account-page feature was switched on, the page's monthly spending calculation failed for those shoppers.

Revision 383534e, which has no empty-month guard, was still running, so switching monthly-spend-feature back on would send account-page requests from shoppers with no purchases this month into the same division-by-zero failure.
Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Shoppers' account page requests failed with server errors, and the account page error rate rose well above its usual level.
Account page requests failed because the spend summary raised a division-by-zero error inside average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py.

Requests reached that function because feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at P3. Flag evaluations went from all off before the onset, to mostly on during the onset minute, to all on afterwards
The deploy of revision 383534e at P2 came at the same instant, so the record does not rule it out; the next step covers it.
The earlier deploy of revision 65279ee (P1): with it in place, account pages were logged as rendering normally and the account page error rate was at its typical level before the onset.

The flag sent requests into code that could not serve a shopper with no purchases this month: the revision deployed at P2 (read at T10 as running on every replica) had taken out the empty-month guard, so the function divides the month's total by the count of purchases recorded this month with nothing to handle a count of none.
monthly-spend-feature was switched on for all traffic at once, at the same instant the revision carrying the changed code behind it was deployed.

No test for a shopper with no purchases this month was seen in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py at the deployed revision. The change that removed the empty-month guard shipped without any seen check catching that the function now fails for that shopper.

The first action tried, rolling back the io-shop deployment, could not be taken: the deployment platform's API server was unavailable, which also put restarting, scaling and every other platform action out of reach.
No on-call person was paged for the alert.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

supported.quote: The failing code path sat behind a feature flag that changed at the same moment as the deploy. Reverting the flag, which did not depend on the unreachable deployment platform, was enough to stop the errors.
